original_question: Fix k >= 2 and assume m is sufficiently large. If G is W_{2k+1}-free, where W_{2k+1} is the odd wheel on 2k+1 vertices, must the extremal graph for lambda(G) depend only on the residue class of m + k(k+1)/2 modulo k, taking the complete join K_k \/ ((m/k) - (k - 1)/2)K_1 in the divisible case and S^{1,l}_{(m-l)/k + (k+3)/2, k} in the other residue classes?
target_in_paper: Section 3, Conjecture 3.44 (the odd-wheel edge-spectral conjecture for W_{2k+1}-free graphs).
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the right forbidden graph family (odd wheels W_{2k+1}), the fixed-parameter regime (k >= 2 fixed, m sufficiently large), the fact that the extremal object is chosen by maximizing the adjacency spectral radius λ(G) among m-edge W_{2k+1}-free graphs, and the residue-class phenomenon modulo k. It also correctly points to the split-graph candidate K_k ∨ ((m/k) - (k - 1)/2)K_1 in the divisible case and to the paper’s residue-class family S^{1,l}_{(m-l)/k + (k+3)/2, k} in the nonzero residue classes.
missing_details: You do not define λ(G) as the adjacency spectral radius of G.
You do not specify the ambient graph class: throughout this literature, the extremal problem is over m-edge F-free graphs without isolated vertices, usually denoted 𝒢(m,F).
You should define the odd wheel explicitly as W_{2k+1} = K_1 ∨ C_{2k}.
The residue parameter l must be introduced explicitly as the unique element of {1,2,...,k-1} such that m + k(k+1)/2 ≡ l (mod k).
The notation S^{1,l}_{n,k} is not defined, so the question is not stand-alone unless that construction is stated or referenced as the paper’s standard residue-class construction.
The question should be phrased as an extremal inequality with an equality characterization, not only as an informal question about whether the extremal graph 'depends only' on a residue class.
You do not say whether the extremal graph is meant to be unique up to isomorphism.
You do not make explicit that 'for sufficiently large m' means: for each fixed k there exists m_0(k) such that the statement holds for all m >= m_0(k).
The join notation ∨ and the complete graph / independent-set notation K_t and sK_1 are left implicit.
The integrality condition in the divisible case is implicit: m + k(k+1)/2 ≡ 0 (mod k) is what makes (m/k) - (k-1)/2 an integer.
refined_question: For a fixed integer k >= 2, does there exist m_0 = m_0(k) such that, for every integer m >= m_0 and every graph G in 𝒢(m, W_{2k+1}) (that is, every W_{2k+1}-free graph with m edges and no isolated vertices), where W_{2k+1} := K_1 ∨ C_{2k}, the adjacency spectral radius λ(G) satisfies λ(G) <= λ(H_{k,m}) with equality if and only if G is isomorphic to H_{k,m}, where H_{k,m} is determined solely by the residue of m + k(k+1)/2 modulo k, namely H_{k,m} = K_k ∨ ((m/k) - (k - 1)/2)K_1 when m + k(k+1)/2 ≡ 0 (mod k), and H_{k,m} = S^{1,l}_{(m-l)/k + (k+3)/2, k} in the paper’s notation when l in {1,...,k-1} is the residue defined by m + k(k+1)/2 ≡ l (mod k)?
justification: The draft is aiming at the survey’s odd-wheel conjecture, not a broader neighboring problem. The decisive features are the forbidden graph W_{2k+1}, the split-graph extremal candidate K_k ∨ ((m/k) - (k - 1)/2)K_1 in the zero-residue case, and the residue-class family S^{1,l}_{...,k} in the nonzero residue classes, which the survey says for wheels 'mirrors' the earlier cycle/theta pattern. The nearby context that makes the question paper-faithful is the Section 3 wheel-graphs discussion together with the almost-bipartite structural theorem later in the same section; that context is why the stand-alone question must quantify over m-edge graphs without isolated vertices, define λ(G), specify the residue parameter l, and ask for an exact extremal inequality with an equality/uniqueness clause rather than only an informal dependence statement.
